source.statement: T-abs-pushup-not-open: on ℝ, the causality with ≪ empty and ≤_U the diagonal plus 0 ≤ 1 in every open U containing 0 and 1 has push-up and is two-sided locally causally open, while J⁺((−1, 1)) = (−1, 1] is not open: not causally open in the future, hence not causally open, and (by the ladder) not absolutely minimal
evidence: 'The closer checks the causality axioms for the stated ≤_U (le_mono: 0 ≤_V 1 needs 0, 1 ∈ V ⊆ U) and names the line. Layer 1: a new module importing LadderLocal (ETT layer).'

questions: Reading of defi:causalite (ETT.tex:237) for this witness: the jump line is a causality in the library's reading (the 'equivalently' form, no gluing axiom, kb/0014) and is not absolutely minimal, necessarily so (by prop:topological_spacetime_absolutely_minimal every witness of locally_causally_open ⇏ causally_open_future fails absolute minimality). Reading taken: the library's, as for deuxPushup (OQ-39). The answer decides whether the [[fails]] entries below say anything about the paper; push_up ⇏ causally_open_future alone holds in both readings (the rational line is absolutely minimal).

prop:topological_spacetime_absolutely_minimal: If M is absolutely minimal and if for every p ∈ M there exists a neighbourhood U of p whose causality is open, then the causality of M is open.

kb_proposals: The jump line (Causal.jumpLine, CausalScaffold.PushUpNotOpen): ≪ empty, ≤_U the diagonal plus 0 ≤_U 1 when 0, 1 ∈ U. Push-up, two-sided locally causally open, GH, strongly causal (open form), time function; not causally open in the future (J⁺((−1,1)) = (−1,1]), not absolutely minimal, not tarentin, not plain. The cheap witness of locally_causally_open ⇏ causally_open_future, necessarily non-absolutely-minimal (prop:topological_spacetime_absolutely_minimal), so it lives in the gluing-free reading only (kb/0014, OQ-18). A link added to the diagonal only in opens containing both ends is a causality (le_mono holds) and is never local.
notes: Layer-1 rule: imports Causal.LadderLocal, Causal.CurvesExtend, Causal.Ladder.Rules (all ETT layer). Checked on a /tmp copy with a run_cmd over the environment's module names: no module under Causal.Minkowski, Causal.Static, Causal.SingularFlat, Causal.Flat, Causal.Model, Causal.Port, Causal.CBG, Causal.LemmaK or Causal.Splitting in the closure. No new mathlib module beyond what those import. No metric notion in any statement (ℝ's order and topology only; mem_nhds_iff_exists_Ioo_subset in two proofs). `lake env lean` and `-DwarningAsError=true` clean (graduation-ready); `lake build CausalScaffold.PushUpNotOpen` rebuilt only this module (1.0 s); #print axioms on jumpLine_separates_causallyOpenFuture, the three _bare theorems, jumpLine_not_absolutelyMinimalOn_top, jumpLine_Jplus_Ioo: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. The scaffold root scaffold/CausalScaffold.lean does not import the module (kb/0025: invisible to the axiom sweep until the master adds it or graduates the file; not edited, outside the dispatch). Names: none of this file's names existed in lean-causal at dispatch time, nor in the two parallel closers' files (ChronalNeighbourBridge.lean, GateLineLocal.lean; checked by grep at the end). Label /beyond goes beyond the target and may be graduated or dropped independently; of its for_keeper entries, 4 (tarentin) is dominated by the existing Causal.spacelikeLine_separates_tarentin_full. No finding against the paper: ETT.tex:698 carries absolute minimality, and this target shows the hypothesis is needed in the library's reading; whether the witness counts at all is OQ-18 (question under labels /line and /separation).
